correctness.rationale: For consecutive weight-two windows separated by t starts, their unordered two-one cyclic-distance labels differ by at most t-1, since changed positions are confined modulo k to an arc of t residues. Cyclic label variation must traverse both 1 and floor(k/2) twice, forcing 2(floor(k/2)-1) non-weight-two windows. The explicit alternating-complementary cyclic gap list contains each gap 1..k-1 and an extra k-1; each gap d has both neighbors at least k-d, giving every position of the two ones in a length-k window. Thus the two proved bounds follow for all k>=4. Direct finite construction and exhaustive k=3,4,5 optimum checks pass. The proof does not assert a general exact optimum.

evidence: Sawada, Williams and Wong (2013), author PDF, introductory example and Theorem 1, prove universal cycles for the entire weight interval, including {1,2} when k>=2. Their construction yields length binom(k,2)+k in that specialization.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The interval-weight construction yields a valid but one-position-longer cyclic cover, and supplies no lower bound implying the sharp linear correction. King et al. provide fixed-weight s-overlap cycles using jumps of at least two, a distinct and longer host model.

value.rationale: Sparse weight-two k-mers form a canonical motif family for constrained de Bruijn covering and binary substring indexing. Pure fixed-weight universal cycles are obstructed, while full weight-{1,2} universal cycles spend k auxiliary windows. The bounds determine the optimal sharp linear correction to the main binomial term up to an absolute constant of at most three, and give an explicit host one character shorter than the natural weight-interval construction. This is a structural infinite-family result, not a routine restatement of existing existence theorems.
